name: Chamunda Electrical Ltd
tagline: Rs 47 Cr micro-cap that operates and maintains transmission substations for Gujarat's state grid - debt-free, ~27% ROE, ~9x earnings, and a GETCO annuity contract that could lift revenue ~two-thirds
business_overview: Chamunda Electrical Ltd (NSE/BSE SME: CHAMUNDA), founded 2013, does operation & maintenance of electrical substations up to 66 KV, testing & commissioning up to 220 KV, erection of EHV-class equipment up to 220 KV, and runs a 1.5 MW solar park in Gujarat. Its principal customer is the Gujarat state transmission utility (GETCO). Promoter holding ~72.6%.
fundamentals_table: GETCO Letter of Award (2026-04-02): Rs 63 Cr, 3-year O&M of 88 units of 66 KV substations (~Rs 21 Cr/yr, ~66% of current annual revenue, annuity-style)
fundamentals_narrative: Unlike most SME leads, the balance sheet here is clean: debt-free, ~27% ROE, ~73% promoter holding, ~9x earnings. The GETCO 3-year O&M award (Rs 63 Cr) is large relative to a ~Rs 31.6 Cr revenue base and is recurring rather than one-off, which improves earnings visibility for a company this small. The business is grid-adjacent - substation O&M and testing demand rises with India's (and Gujarat's) transmission capex cycle. The constraints are structural to the size: a ~Rs 47 Cr market cap means thin liquidity and limited disclosure; revenue is heavily concentrated on a single state utility (GETCO) in a single state; and substation O&M is a low-value-add, labour-and-tender-driven activity with periodic recompete risk. No independent verification of FY26 numbers or the contract beyond the Sovrenn lead and screener data.

value_chain.theme: Grid / transmission (substation O&M and testing services)
value_chain.position: Services layer - operates, maintains, tests and commissions transmission substations for a state grid utility; not an equipment maker
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Skilled substation-O&M manpower and utility empanelment; low capital intensity
value_chain.note: Grid/transmission is a priority-1 theme (record global and Indian grid capex). Chamunda's exposure is genuine but indirect and low-margin: more substations built means more O&M and testing tenders, but the value in the chain accrues to transformer/switchgear makers and T&D EPC contractors, not to a small O&M services vendor. The GETCO annuity is the concrete evidence of demand pull-through.

GETCO 3-year O&M award (Rs 63 Cr) is large vs a ~Rs 31.6 Cr revenue base and is recurring - a concrete, size-transforming catalyst
Grid-adjacent (priority-1 transmission theme): substation O&M/testing demand tracks India's transmission capex cycle

Small solar (1.5 MW) and testing lines add little; growth beyond GETCO is unproven
verdict_headline: Cleanest of this run's SME leads - debt-free, high-ROE micro-cap with a concrete annuity catalyst - scored 10x-in-2-3-years at Low-Medium, unconfirmed pending GETCO revenue conversion

Per the trailing-average-vs-live-inflection rule: decent trailing returns + a strong specific catalyst (contract ~66% of current revenue, annuity) + a tiny base -> 10x-in-2-3-years at Low-Medium with an 'unconfirmed' caveat (the award must actually phase into billed revenue and hold on renewal)
